split_reasoning: Product questions are answered both during live customer contacts and in response to written inquiries.

parts.text: Answer a customer's product, price, availability, use, or credit-term question during a live contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The customer waits while the representative answers.
parts.unit_reasoning: The answer to the customer's inquiry is the output of this step, rather than a complete sale.
parts.work_item: one customer inquiry answered during a live contact
parts.start: customer asks a question
parts.end: answer is communicated to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: Recommendations, sales contacts, and quotations can include answers to product questions but also have distinct purposes.

parts.text: Answer a written customer question about products, prices, availability, uses, or credit terms.
parts.type_reasoning: A written inquiry receives a response without the customer waiting in a live contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: The written answer is sent and relied on as a whole.
parts.start: written inquiry received
parts.end: answer sent to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: A written answer may include a recommendation or a price or term quotation, but those tasks also cover other work.

notes: Shares depend on the sales channel and customer mix.

split_reasoning: Recommendations are made both in live customer conversations and in written follow-up.

parts.text: Recommend products suited to a customer's needs during a live contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The recommendation is provided while the customer is present or on the line.
parts.unit_reasoning: One recommendation addresses a particular customer's expressed needs.
parts.work_item: one product recommendation communicated during a customer contact
parts.start: customer's needs or interests are discussed
parts.end: suitable product options are recommended to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: Answering questions and demonstrating products can support a recommendation but are not identical to selecting suitable products.

parts.text: Send a written product recommendation based on a customer's needs and interests.
parts.type_reasoning: The recommendation is prepared and sent outside a live contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: The customer receives the recommendation as a complete response.
parts.start: customer's requirements or request received
parts.end: recommended options sent to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: A written recommendation may answer questions or accompany a bid, but each task has a distinct output.

notes: Shares vary with the extent of written follow-up.

split_reasoning: Demonstrating features and soliciting orders are elements of the same live sales contact.

parts.text: Contact a regular or prospective customer to demonstrate products, explain features, and solicit an order.
parts.type_reasoning: The work is a live sales interaction with a customer, including product explanations and solicitation.
parts.unit_reasoning: A single sales contact is the relevant unit, independent of any subsequent order form.
parts.start: representative connects with the customer
parts.end: product discussion and order solicitation conclude
parts.overlap_reasoning: The contact may include questions, recommendations, samples, or quotations, each of which also occurs separately.

notes: Preparing an order form or forwarding an order is covered by other statements.

split_reasoning: Prices and terms are quoted both while customers wait and through written quotations prepared afterward.

parts.text: Estimate or quote prices, terms, warranties, or delivery dates during a customer contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The estimate or quotation is communicated while the customer is present or on the line.
parts.unit_reasoning: One quotation responds to a customer's request and can cover several commercial terms.
parts.work_item: one price or terms quotation given during a customer contact
parts.start: customer requests pricing or terms
parts.end: estimate or terms are communicated to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: The quotation can answer a customer question or form part of a sales contact, but is not the same as a prepared bid or contract negotiation.

parts.text: Prepare and send a written estimate or quotation of prices and commercial terms.
parts.type_reasoning: The quotation is assembled and sent outside a live contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: The quotation is the document the customer uses to assess the proposed sale.
parts.work_item: one written price or terms quotation
parts.start: customer requirements and quotation request received
parts.end: quotation sent to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: A tailored estimate or bid can include the same quotation work, while also requiring additional customer-specific preparation.

notes: The live and written shares vary with the complexity of the sale.

split_reasoning: Post-sale support is provided both in live consultations and through subsequent written or back-office resolution.

parts.text: Consult with a customer live about a post-sale problem or support need.
parts.type_reasoning: The customer is present or on the line while the representative provides support.
parts.unit_reasoning: One support contact addresses the customer's current problem or question.
parts.start: customer raises a post-sale issue
parts.end: support or next steps are communicated during the contact
parts.overlap_reasoning: Support may include product answers or coordination of delivery, but those tasks also occur outside post-sale problem resolution.

parts.text: Resolve or respond to a post-sale support issue outside a live customer contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The representative works from an inquiry or follow-up task without the customer waiting live.
parts.unit_reasoning: The response or resolution for one issue is communicated back to the customer.
parts.work_item: one post-sale support issue resolved or answered
parts.start: written issue or follow-up request received
parts.end: resolution or status communicated to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: Resolution can involve delivery coordination or answering product questions, but also covers other post-sale issues.

notes: Some issues require multiple contacts; the shares are approximate.

split_reasoning: Drawings, standalone estimates, and bids are different customer-facing deliverables, although an estimate can be included in a bid.

parts.text: Prepare a drawing to meet a customer's specific needs.
parts.type_reasoning: A completed drawing is a distinct artifact for customer or internal review.
parts.unit_reasoning: A drawing for one customer requirement is reviewed as a whole.
parts.start: customer specifications received
parts.end: drawing completed and sent for review
parts.checked_by: customer and sales or technical team
parts.overlap_reasoning: A drawing can accompany a bid or support a product recommendation, but it is a distinct deliverable.

parts.text: Prepare a standalone estimate to meet a customer's specific needs.
parts.type_reasoning: The estimate is a completed document sent or presented to the customer.
parts.unit_reasoning: One estimate covers a defined customer requirement.
parts.start: customer requirements and estimate request received
parts.end: estimate completed and sent to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: A written quotation can be the same estimate, though the quotation task also covers less tailored and live quotes.

parts.text: Prepare a bid to meet a customer's specific needs.
parts.type_reasoning: A bid is a discrete proposal submitted for the customer's consideration.
parts.unit_reasoning: The bid package for one opportunity is submitted and evaluated as a whole.
parts.start: bid request and customer specifications received
parts.end: bid completed and submitted
parts.overlap_reasoning: A bid includes pricing or terms and may incorporate product recommendations, but it has a broader submission purpose.

notes: Shares vary substantially by product line; an estimate included in a bid is part of that bid rather than an additional item.

split_reasoning: Physically providing samples or printed catalogs differs from sending electronic catalog material.

parts.text: Prepare and provide physical product samples or printed catalogs to a customer.
parts.type_reasoning: Handling, packing, or delivering physical samples and catalogs requires hands-on work.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Samples and catalogs may be provided during a sales demonstration, but they can also be supplied separately.

parts.text: Send a customer an electronic product catalog or requested catalog materials.
parts.type_reasoning: An electronic catalog is selected and sent as a discrete customer-facing output.
parts.unit_reasoning: One response supplies the materials requested for a customer.
parts.work_item: one electronic catalog or catalog package sent
parts.start: customer request or need for catalog material identified
parts.end: catalog material sent to the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: Catalogs can support product answers and sales contacts, but supplying the material is a separate step.

notes: The physical and electronic shares depend on the products and sales channel.

split_reasoning: Directories, referrals, organizations, and events are alternative sources for the same output: identified prospects.

parts.text: Identify a prospective customer using available leads, directories, or business contacts.
parts.type_reasoning: Prospecting produces identifiable leads that can be followed up by sales staff.
parts.unit_reasoning: A prospect record or lead is the unit handed into sales follow-up.
parts.start: lead source or business contact identified
parts.end: prospect details captured for follow-up
parts.overlap_reasoning: Identifying a prospect precedes contacting that prospect, while obtaining credit information is a separate assessment.

notes: Networking and event attendance are treated as sources of leads rather than separate deliverables.

split_reasoning: Delivery and installation are related logistical activities coordinated for a customer order.

parts.text: Arrange and direct delivery and, where needed, installation for a customer order.
parts.type_reasoning: Coordination produces an agreed delivery or installation arrangement for downstream teams and the customer.
parts.unit_reasoning: The arrangement for one order is the unit passed to the delivery or installation team.
parts.work_item: one order's delivery and installation arrangement
parts.start: order and delivery or installation requirements received
parts.end: schedule and instructions confirmed with the parties responsible
parts.checked_by: customer and delivery or installation team
parts.overlap_reasoning: Delivery coordination can be part of post-sale support, but routine arrangements and other support problems are distinct.

notes: The target concerns arranging and directing, not physically installing the equipment.

split_reasoning: Market conditions, innovations, and competitors are different inputs to the same continuing market-monitoring activity.

parts.text: Capture and communicate a relevant market, product, or competitor development.
parts.type_reasoning: The continuing monitoring activity can produce discrete market-intelligence updates for the sales team.
parts.unit_reasoning: An update on a notable development is a manageable item that colleagues can use.
parts.work_item: one market or competitor intelligence update
parts.start: relevant market or competitor information becomes available
parts.end: key finding recorded or communicated to the sales team
parts.overlap_reasoning: Market intelligence may inform sales reports or prospecting, but those statements cover different outputs.

notes: Some monitoring is informal and used only to stay current; not every observation produces a shared update.

split_reasoning: Sales budgets, sales reports, sales records, and expense reports are distinct administrative outputs.

parts.text: Prepare a sales budget.
parts.type_reasoning: A budget is a discrete planning document submitted for review.
parts.unit_reasoning: One period's sales budget is reviewed as a whole.
parts.start: budget period and planning inputs established
parts.end: budget submitted for review
parts.overlap_reasoning: No other listed statement describes preparation of the sales budget.

parts.text: Prepare a sales report.
parts.type_reasoning: A report is a discrete document used by management.
parts.unit_reasoning: One report covers a defined reporting period or request.
parts.start: reporting period or request established
parts.end: report completed and submitted
parts.overlap_reasoning: A report may draw on market monitoring, but reporting sales and monitoring market developments are not the same activity.

parts.text: Update a sales record.
parts.type_reasoning: Each maintained sales record is relied on by the sales organization.
parts.unit_reasoning: A record update captures a defined sale or sales activity for later use.
parts.start: sale or sales activity information becomes available
parts.end: record saved in the sales system or files
parts.overlap_reasoning: Sales records can use information from orders and contracts, but maintaining the record is not the same as preparing or forwarding them.

parts.text: Prepare and file an expense account report.
parts.type_reasoning: An expense report is submitted as a distinct claim for review.
parts.unit_reasoning: A report with its supporting expenses is reviewed and processed as a whole.
parts.start: expenses and receipts accumulated for submission
parts.end: expense report filed
parts.overlap_reasoning: No other listed statement describes expense reporting.

notes: The examples are not exhaustive; shares depend on administrative requirements.

split_reasoning: Obtaining credit information is one assessment-support activity, regardless of the source consulted.

parts.text: Obtain credit information about a prospective customer.
parts.type_reasoning: The information gathered for a prospect is a discrete input to credit review.
parts.unit_reasoning: A credit-information package for one prospect is passed to or used by the person assessing credit.
parts.work_item: one prospective customer's credit information obtained
parts.start: prospective customer identified for credit inquiry
parts.end: available credit information gathered and made available for review
parts.overlap_reasoning: Credit information may inform quoted terms, but collecting it is not itself quoting terms or negotiating payment.

split_reasoning: Forwarding orders is one activity regardless of the transmission method.

parts.text: Forward a customer's order to the manufacturer.
parts.type_reasoning: Each order is transmitted for manufacturer processing outside a live customer contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: The order is the unit received and processed by the manufacturer.
parts.work_item: one order forwarded to a manufacturer
parts.start: completed order available for transmission
parts.end: order sent to the manufacturer
parts.overlap_reasoning: Preparing an order form precedes forwarding it and produces a different step output.

split_reasoning: Physical stock checks, computer-based stock checks, and placing replenishment orders are different activities.

parts.text: Physically check merchandise stock levels.
parts.type_reasoning: Counting or inspecting stock at its location requires hands-on work away from a computer.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Checking stock can inform a retail display restock, but inventory checking and assembling displays are not identical.

parts.text: Review recorded merchandise stock levels.
parts.type_reasoning: A stock review produces a discrete assessment of recorded availability or replenishment need.
parts.unit_reasoning: A review of an item or stock group yields a result used to decide whether to reorder.
parts.start: inventory records or stock alert available
parts.end: stock level reviewed and replenishment need identified
parts.overlap_reasoning: Availability answers may use the same stock information, but a stock review also supports inventory control.

parts.text: Place a merchandise replenishment order when needed.
parts.type_reasoning: A replenishment order is a distinct output sent to a supplier or manufacturer.
parts.unit_reasoning: One reorder is processed as a complete purchasing request.
parts.start: replenishment need identified
parts.end: reorder submitted to the supplier
parts.overlap_reasoning: A reorder may be forwarded to a manufacturer, but forwarding also covers customer orders and does not necessarily include deciding and preparing a replenishment order.

notes: The mix of physical and system checks depends on the representative's inventory responsibilities.

split_reasoning: Building and stocking displays is physical work, while recommending displays or promotions is advisory work delivered live or in writing.

parts.text: Plan, assemble, and stock a retail product display.
parts.type_reasoning: Assembling and stocking a display requires hands-on work in the store.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Display stocking may involve checking stock and may follow negotiation over shelf positioning, but neither is the same as building the display.

parts.text: Recommend display, promotional, or advertising arrangements to a retailer during a live contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The retailer is present while the representative discusses the recommendations.
parts.unit_reasoning: One recommendation addresses the retailer's display or promotional needs during the contact.
parts.work_item: one retail display or promotion recommendation given live
parts.start: retailer discusses display or promotional needs
parts.end: recommendation communicated to the retailer
parts.overlap_reasoning: A recommendation may lead to negotiation over exposure, but recommending an arrangement and negotiating its acceptance are distinct.

parts.text: Send a retailer written recommendations for displays, promotions, or advertising.
parts.type_reasoning: The recommendation is prepared and sent outside a live contact.
parts.unit_reasoning: The written recommendation is supplied to the retailer as a complete response.
parts.work_item: one written retail display or promotion recommendation
parts.start: retailer's needs or request identified
parts.end: recommendation sent to the retailer
parts.overlap_reasoning: Written recommendations can support exposure negotiations, but they also serve retailers without a negotiation.

notes: Shares depend on whether representatives personally merchandise stores or mainly advise retailers.

split_reasoning: Negotiating shelf positioning and advertising are alternative subjects of the same retailer negotiation.

parts.text: Negotiate with a retail merchant for better product exposure.
parts.type_reasoning: The core work is live negotiation and persuasion with the merchant.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Negotiation may include display or promotional recommendations, but each activity also occurs independently.

notes: Any resulting display work is covered separately by task 8128.

split_reasoning: Sales contracts and order forms are different documents; order forms are prepared both during customer contacts and afterward.

parts.text: Prepare a sales contract for a customer.
parts.type_reasoning: A contract is a discrete document prepared for customer and company review or signature.
parts.unit_reasoning: The contract for one sale is reviewed and signed as a whole.
parts.start: agreed or proposed sale terms available
parts.end: contract prepared and sent for review or signature
parts.checked_by: customer and sales manager or legal team
parts.overlap_reasoning: Contract preparation records negotiated or quoted terms but is not the same as negotiating or quoting them.

parts.text: Prepare an order form while the customer is present or on the line.
parts.type_reasoning: The form is completed during a live customer contact while the customer waits.
parts.unit_reasoning: One completed order form captures the customer's order within the contact.
parts.work_item: one order form prepared during a customer contact
parts.start: customer gives order details
parts.end: order details entered and confirmed with the customer
parts.overlap_reasoning: Soliciting an order can lead to form preparation, but the sales contact and form are different steps.

parts.text: Prepare an order form from customer instructions outside a live contact.
parts.type_reasoning: The order form is completed from written instructions or after the customer contact ends.
parts.unit_reasoning: One completed form is passed to order processing or forwarding.
parts.work_item: one order form prepared outside a customer contact
parts.start: customer order details received
parts.end: order form completed for processing
parts.overlap_reasoning: Forwarding the completed order is a subsequent step rather than the same output.

notes: Shares and the extent of live form preparation vary by sales process.

split_reasoning: Contract details and payment terms are subjects of the same negotiation.

parts.text: Negotiate contract and payment details with a customer.
parts.type_reasoning: The central work is live negotiation between the representative and customer.
parts.overlap_reasoning: Negotiation can include discussing quoted terms and precedes contract preparation, but those tasks also cover separate work.

notes: Formal preparation of the resulting contract is coded under task 20267.
